slides.title: Welcome to FIRST LEGO League
slides.body: This season, our team will build robots, solve real problems, practice teamwork, and compete in the 2026-2027 BIOGLOW Challenge.

slides.title: What is FIRST?
slides.body: FIRST is a global robotics community that helps students build science, technology, engineering, and teamwork skills through hands-on challenges. The goal is not just to win. The goal is to learn how engineers think, work together, and improve the world around them.

slides.title: What is FLL?
slides.body: FIRST LEGO League is a robotics program where students use LEGO Education tools to design, build, program, research, test, present, and compete. Teams work like a small engineering group: everyone has a role, everyone contributes, and every idea can become part of the solution.

slides.title: FLL Core Values
slides.body:
Core Values are how we work together.

Discovery: We explore new skills and ideas.
Innovation: We use creativity and persistence to solve problems.
Impact: We apply what we learn to improve our world.
Inclusion: We respect each other and embrace our differences.
Teamwork: We are stronger when we work together.
Fun: We enjoy and celebrate what we do.

slides.title: The Four Main Parts of FLL
slides.body:
FLL teams are evaluated in four connected areas:

Robot Game: score points with an autonomous robot on the mission field.
Robot Design: explain how the robot, attachments, programs, and strategy improved.
Innovation Project: research a real-world problem and create a useful solution.
Core Values: show teamwork, inclusion, discovery, innovation, impact, and fun in everything we do.

slides.title: What is BIOGLOW About?
slides.body: BIOGLOW is the 2026-2027 FIRST LEGO League season. Teams will explore the vibrancy of the world's ecosystems and think about how living things, habitats, technology, creativity, and innovation connect. The challenge releases worldwide on August 4, 2026.

slides.title: Our Season Mindset
slides.body: We will ask good questions, test before we assume, keep track of our ideas, learn from failure, and help our teammates get better. A strong FLL team does not need one genius. It needs a group that listens, builds, shares, and improves together.
